userStories.title: Implement read-only gold-DB open path
userStories.description: As a developer, I need an openGoldDb() function that applies four independent read-only guards and throws at startup if PRAGMA query_only is not 1, so the 54 GB gold DB cannot be mutated by the API/UI/cache.
acceptanceCriteria: File ~/signal-console/packages/db/src/open.ts exists
Exports function openGoldDb(path: string) using better-sqlite3
Implementation passes URI 'file:${path}?mode=ro' AND options { readonly: true, fileMustExist: true } to the Database constructor
Implementation runs PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000 and PRAGMA query_only = ON, then reads PRAGMA query_only back; throws Error('gold DB connection is not query_only') if the returned value is not 1
Default GOLD_DB_PATH constant points to a path matching ~/signal-console/data/signal-console.sqlite (NOT ~/nba-predict/data/...)
Grep across the repo shows zero occurrences of the string 'nba-predict/data/signal-console.sqlite' outside the allow-listed docs
Unit test asserts that INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and CREATE TEMP VIEW statements against the returned handle each throw an error
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
Running 'pnpm verify:no-stale-plan' exits 0
userStories.notes: better-sqlite3 does not enable `file:` URI parsing by default; the PRD §11.1 example code is incomplete. open.ts sets `process.env.SQLITE_USE_URI = '1'` at module load to make guard #1 (the `?mode=ro` URI) actually effective. The native addon loads lazily on first `new Database()` call and calls `sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_URI, 1)` once based on this env var. Guard #2 (`readonly: true`) is independent of this and continues to enforce SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY. Future db-package modules (US-005+) that import better-sqlite3 must import this module first or replicate the env-var setting before their own `new Database()` calls, since `std::call_once` makes the URI config a one-shot per process.

userStories.title: Board-MAD contract tests at K=6.0
userStories.description: As a developer, I need contract tests locking in the research report's K=6.0 outcomes so future drift is immediately caught.
acceptanceCriteria: File ~/signal-console/packages/detectors/src/board-mad/__tests__/canonical.test.ts exists

Test 'hartenstein fires at K=6': running board-mad on the nba-0042500222 fixture with kMad=6.0 produces a fire whose bucket_start equals 2026-05-08T03:12:00Z and whose bucket_end equals 2026-05-08T03:13:00Z (watcher confirmation ≈ T+23 s after event 03:12:36.8Z)
Test 'reaves no-fire at K=6': running board-mad on both nba-0042500223 and nba-0042500224 fixtures with kMad=6.0 produces zero fires within ±5 min of event 2026-05-12T04:51:40.2Z

Test '64-game mean fires at K=6': running board-mad across the 64-game PBP fixture set with kMad=6.0 and weighting='equal' produces mean fires per game in [8.3, 10.3]; with weighting='volume' produces mean in [7.6, 9.6]
Test names cite event timestamp and bucket timestamp explicitly so future readers cannot conflate detector output (bucket-start) with watcher confirmation (bucket-end)
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes:
Reaves no-fire semantics: AC text says "zero fires within +/-5 min of event," which under a literal bucket-start filter would FAIL because the TS detector produces a fire at 2026-05-12T04:50:00Z (bucket-end 04:51:00Z, 40.2s before the event) on nba-0042500224. The TS port matches Python board_signal_v2.py exactly (verified: both produce 7 fires for game 224 in its PBP window, including this 04:50:00 fire). Python research uses fire_after semantics, which only counts fires whose bucket-end is AFTER the event (the live watcher cannot attribute a pre-event spike to the event). CLAUDE.md anchors the canonical Reaves outcome to the research report (board_signal_v2.py). The test therefore filters fires by bucketEnd > event AND bucketStart within +/-5 min; a future iteration that reverts to literal bucket-start semantics will silently break the canonical contract.

PBP fixture count: AC says "64-game PBP fixture set"; the gold DB now has 66 distinct PBP-anchored games (DB has grown since the research report). The test asserts >= 64 to remain valid as data continues to grow. Mean fires/game across all 66 fixtures (5-min PBP pre-buffer + 1-min post-buffer): 9.80 equal, 9.17 volume (in tolerance [8.3, 10.3] and [7.6, 9.6]). Python research means with strict PBP MIN/MAX windows: 9.12 equal, 8.58 volume; the pre-buffer that seeds the trailing baseline shifts the means slightly upward, both still within tolerance.

Fixture directory size: 4.6 MB total (66 files), under the 5 MB soft cap noted in US-010 progress.

userStories.notes: Server lives at apps/api/src/server.ts; exports buildServer() (used by tests via Fastify inject) AND starts when invoked directly (gated by `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === resolve(process.argv[1])` so importing for tests does NOT start a listener). Fastify v5.8 + @fastify/swagger v9.7 + @fastify/swagger-ui v5.2. Two env vars: SIGNAL_CONSOLE_API_PORT (default 4100, validated 1-65535) and SIGNAL_CONSOLE_API_HOST (default localhost). Cold-start verified: from pnpm start to `{"msg":"ready"}` log emission both listener bind lines fire in the same millisecond as the ready log (well under 2s on darwin-arm64). GOTCHA: `@typescript-eslint/return-await:always` flagged `return app;` inside the async buildServer because FastifyInstance is THENABLE (`await app` triggers `app.ready()`). Fix is `return await app;` which both satisfies the rule and gives callers a ready-to-inject server. The same thenable-ness means tests do not need a separate app.ready() call after buildServer(), though keeping it is harmless (idempotent). Second gotcha: arrow handlers like `() => app.swagger()` also trip return-await because Fastify route handlers are contextually typed `Promise<unknown> | unknown`; the workaround is a block body using reply.send: `(_req, reply) => { reply.send(app.swagger()); }` — no return value, no rule fire. Swagger doc: openapi=3.1.0, info.title="Signal Console API", info.version=0.0.0, one server entry at http://localhost:4100. /docs/ serves the Swagger UI HTML; smoke test asserts [200,302] there to absorb the trailing-slash redirect Fastify-Swagger-UI sometimes does. Test pattern: beforeEach/afterEach builds + closes a fresh app per test; ctx.current handle pattern (no FastifyInstance global) to avoid linter complaints about uninitialised vars. Logger format is pino JSON; the literal `"msg":"ready"` substring is what future US-017 ready-route tests might grep for if needed.

userStories.description: As an operator, I need a Fastify plugin that validates the X-Signal-Token header against the contents of ~/.signal-console/token on each request, so the public tunnel cannot be hit anonymously and token rotation does not require restarts.
acceptanceCriteria: File ~/signal-console/apps/api/src/plugins/auth.ts exists and exports a Fastify plugin
Plugin reads the current token from ~/.signal-console/token on each request (or with at most a 1-second TTL cache); editing the file takes effect without restart
Requests missing X-Signal-Token or with a wrong token return 401 with body { error: 'unauthorized' }
Requests to /v1/health/live are exempt from the token check
Unit test asserts 401 on missing header, 401 on wrong token, 200 on correct token; test mutates a temp token file mid-test and asserts the new token takes effect without server restart
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Plugin at apps/api/src/plugins/auth.ts wrapped with fastify-plugin (v5.1) so the onRequest hook propagates to the parent scope and protects all top-level routes (without fp, the hook is encapsulated and routes registered after the plugin at the root context don't see it). Token file is read with `fs.promises.readFile` on cache miss; TTL cache default is 1000 ms. The cache is invalidated by an ttl-only check (Date.now()-fetchedAt < ttl). Future tightening (e.g. mtime invalidation for sub-second rotation) is additive. AuthPluginOptions accepts `tokenPath`, `exemptPaths`, `cacheTtlMs` overrides; tests pass cacheTtlMs=0 so rotation takes effect on the next request without sleeping. server.ts buildServer() now accepts BuildServerOptions { auth?: AuthPluginOptions } and forwards them to the plugin. GOTCHA: `return reply` from an async onRequest hook fires `@typescript-eslint/return-await: always` because FastifyReply is thenable (same root cause as US-015's FastifyInstance gotcha). The fix matches the US-015 pattern: rewrite the hook to NOT return reply — use a single `await reply.code(401).send(...)` call and let it short-circuit. The await also satisfies no-floating-promises because reply.send() returns a thenable. The /v1/health/live exemption is implemented by exempt-path list comparison after stripping the querystring (`url.split('?')[0]`); the route doesn't have to exist for the exemption to work — an unregistered exempt path returns 404 from the router, not 401 from auth, which is exactly what the test verifies. The existing scaffold test (server.test.ts) was updated to create a temp token file and pass `x-signal-token` on its inject() calls — once auth is wired, /openapi.json is also protected per PRD §FR-15 ('All routes require header X-Signal-Token... except /v1/health/live'). Default tokenPath is `join(homedir(), '.signal-console', 'token')` — never written to a code constant verbatim. If a future story needs to expose auth to a non-Fastify caller (e.g., the worker package), extract readExpectedToken/cache to a tiny standalone module; today it's closure-local.

userStories.notes:
Routes live at apps/api/src/routes/health.ts as a Fastify plugin (FastifyPluginAsync<HealthRoutesOptions>) accepting an optional goldDbPath; default is GOLD_DB_PATH from @signal-console/db. server.ts now registers healthRoutes AFTER auth+swagger so the routes are auto-described by @fastify/swagger. /v1/health/live is auth-exempt (DEFAULT_EXEMPT_PATHS in plugins/auth.ts already lists it) and the route handler does ZERO DB access — verified by a test that points goldDbPath at a missing file and still gets 200. /v1/health/ready is NOT exempt per FR-15 (only live is); it opens the gold DB via openGoldDb(path), runs `SELECT 1`, closes in finally, then 200 { ok: true } or 503 { ok: false, reason } on any throw. Reason string uses err.message when err is an Error else String(err) via a tiny reasonFrom helper to avoid `as` casts. Route tags use Fastify's per-route `schema.tags: ['internal']` which @fastify/swagger v9 transcribes into openapi.paths[path].get.tags — the 5th health test asserts both routes have 'internal' in their tags list. Added @signal-console/db@workspace:* + better-sqlite3@^12.4.0 + @types/better-sqlite3 as devDeps to apps/api (better-sqlite3 only for the seed-real-gold-db test helper). 

ESLINT GOTCHA logged for future API stories: under `consistent-type-assertions: never` + `no-unsafe-assignment`, the natural pattern `const v = body['paths']` returns `unknown` (from Record<string, unknown>), and then `if (!isRecord(v)) throw` narrows it. BUT inside a NESTED FUNCTION that captures the narrowed variable, TS sometimes drops the narrowing or emits `any`-typed lookups (the symptom is `no-unsafe-assignment: 'error typed value'` on `const entry = paths[path]`). Also: explicitly annotating `const v: unknown = body['paths']` ERASES the subsequent isRecord narrowing because the annotation forces the wider type. The working pattern is: do not annotate, let isRecord narrow inline, AND pass the narrowed Record<string, unknown> into the helper as an explicit parameter (`tagsForGet(allPaths: Record<string, unknown>, path)`) so the parameter type stays Record<string, unknown> inside the helper. Reuse this pattern in US-018/019/020 when poking at openapi or other unknown-shaped response bodies.

userStories.notes: Service module 126 LOC; route handler 151 LOC (both within the relaxed budgets noted in PRD §13/§25). Both routes inline the v_games CTE via `WITH v_games AS (${v_games}) ...`. Service exposes parseIsoDuration + isValidIsoDuration; the route's Zod schema uses `isValidIsoDuration` in a `.refine()` so invalid `since` produces a clean 400 with the Zod error message. JSON-Schema response stanzas (gameRowJsonSchema, listResponseSchema, errorResponseSchema) are written as `as const` literals — fast-json-stringify strips properties not declared on the response schema, so the gameRow schema lists every column the service projects including `status` which can be null (`{ type: ["string", "null"] }`). Test pattern mirrors health.test.ts: `seedGoldDb(path, games[])` builds a tiny writable SQLite mirroring the gold-DB shape (games + game_states + idx_game_states_game_captured), then the route opens it read-only via openGoldDb. Eslint trap: `Array.isArray(value)` narrows to `any[]`, which then trips `no-unsafe-assignment` on `arr[0]`; introduce a local `isUnknownArray(v): v is readonly unknown[]` helper that returns `Array.isArray(v)` to keep the narrowing at `unknown[]`. Also: under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`, the Zod query schema's `sport?: string | undefined` doesn't satisfy `sport?: string` — declare ListGamesArgs.sport as `sport?: string | undefined` explicitly. Response shape is `{ games: [...] }` (wrapper object) to leave room for pagination metadata later without a breaking change. Routes open openGoldDb per request and close in a finally block; SQLite open is fast (sub-ms) so this is fine for the expected load. participant JSON is exposed as raw strings (homeParticipantJson / awayParticipantJson) — UI parses with its own validators in US-024.

userStories.title: Settings route (/v1/settings)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need GET /v1/settings returning DB diagnostics + log tail so the Settings UI has everything in one call.
acceptanceCriteria: File ~/signal-console/apps/api/src/routes/settings.ts exists

GET /v1/settings returns a Zod-typed body containing: db (path, sizeBytes, walBytes, pageCount, pageSize, lastModified, mode), cacheDb (path, sizeBytes, pageCount), sources (object keyed by source name with lastSyncAt, lastError, rateLimitCooldown) OR { ingestPaused: true, lastKnown: {...} } when no heartbeat file exists, errors (array of up to 200 most-recent structured log entries with level and message), about (appVersion, detectorVersions, dbSchemaVersion)
Route tagged 'internal' in /openapi.json
Route response time is under 100 ms when measured against the moved gold DB (no full scans; only PRAGMA reads)
Unit tests assert: mode reports 'read-only'; missing heartbeat file produces ingestPaused: true
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes:
Service module apps/api/src/services/settings.ts opens the gold DB once via openGoldDb (read PRAGMA page_count + page_size + user_version) and the cache DB via better-sqlite3 readonly handle (PRAGMA page_count); all sizes/mtimes come from fs.statSync. Mode is 'read-only' on successful open or 'error' (with openError) when openGoldDb throws — guaranteed since openGoldDb enforces query_only=ON. Heartbeat default at ~/signal-console/apps/worker/data/heartbeat.json — when absent the response is { ingestPaused: true, lastKnown: {} } per AC; when present we parse { sources: { name: { lastSyncAt, lastError, rateLimitCooldown } } } into bySource. Log file default at ~/signal-console/apps/api/data/api.log; we readFileSync the whole file, split + parse pino JSON lines, drop nulls (blank/non-JSON), then slice the last maxErrors (default 200). About block exposes appVersion (read once from apps/api/package.json at route registration via readDefaultAppVersion()), detectorVersions from the registry (currently empty — board-mad isn't registered yet), and dbSchemaVersion from PRAGMA user_version. Response schema is large but follows the same fast-json-stringify pattern from health.ts/games.ts — pure JSON Schema literals as const, no Zod-to-JSON-Schema dep added.

GOTCHAS for future iterations: (1) Don't alias ReturnType<typeof openGoldDb> as GoldDbHandle alongside Database.Database — eslint's @typescript-eslint/no-duplicate-type-constituents flags the union because they're structurally identical. Use Database.Database directly (the dep is already in apps/api's devDeps for tests). The pattern from scripts/verify-queries.ts and apps/api/src/services/games.ts deliberately keeps better-sqlite3 out of the import graph, but here we already need it for the cache DB handle so import it directly. (2) Tail-after-parse, not tail-then-parse. text.split("\n") on a file ending with "\n" produces a trailing empty element; map+filter drops it but if you slice BEFORE filtering you get 199/200 entries. Fix: parse first, filter nulls, THEN slice(-max). (3) exactOptionalPropertyTypes:true bites again — passing an optional field through to a downstream interface forces conditional spread: `...(maxErrors !== undefined ? { maxErrors } : {})` — see route plugin's readSettings call. Plain `maxErrors,` would type-error because `maxErrors?: number` ≠ `maxErrors: number | undefined`. (4) New barrel export from @signal-console/db: CACHE_DB_PATH + openCacheDb + runMigrations. The settings.test.ts now seeds the cache DB via runMigrations(new Database(path)) to get a non-empty pageCount; same pattern any future cache-touching test can use.
